extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art, literature, and poetry translators
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted material pertains to Tolstoy's statements about the purpose/destiny of art (ethical/didactic criteria for art) and to translator guidance for rendering French poems into English. Also includes transcription/formatting instructions for e-texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destiny/purpose of art: evoke brotherhood and union
rubrics_metrics.description: The destiny of art in our time is to transmit from the realm of reason to the realm of feeling the truth that well-being for men consists in being united together, and to set up, in place of the existing reign of force, that kingdom of God, i.e. of love, which we all recognise to be the highest aim of human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By evoking, under imaginary conditions, the feeling of brotherhood and love, religious art will train men to experience those same feelings under similar circumstances in actual life; it will lay in the souls of men the rails along which the actions of those whom art thus educates will naturally pass. Universal art, by uniting the most different people in one common feeling, by destroying separation, will educate people to union, will show them, not by reason but by life itself, the joy of universal union reaching beyond the bounds set by life. The task for Christian art is to establish brotherly union among men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation priority: preserve sense over form
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of these renderings has been to keep as close to the originals as the obscurity of meaning allowed. The sense (or absence of sense) has therefore been more considered than the form of the verses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translator's stated policy: when rendering French poems into English, prioritize conveying the meaning (or lack thereof) rather than strictly preserving original verse form or formal features. (Translations in Appendices I., II., and IV. are by Louise Maude.)

rubrics_metrics.name: E-text transcription conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcriber's Notes specify how typographic features from the printed edition are to be encoded in the e-text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions used on this e-text: italics are enclosed by underscores (_italics_), boldface by equals signs (=bold=), and footnotes moved to follow the chapters in which they are referenced. These are production rules for preparing readable electronic versions and should be followed when producing or evaluating Project Gutenberg-style transcriptions.
